consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... she has astigmatism, which means her eyes don't focus properly on things. It's been a challenge for her, especially when trying to read or watch TV. We're really worried about how this might affect her learning.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She had fluid in her ear for a while, and we were so scared it would affect her hearing permanently. Luckily, after treatment, everything seems back to normal now. But I still get anxious whenever she complains about her ear.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has been an issue for her since she started eating solid foods. Some foods are just too hard for her to manage. We've had to adjust her diet accordingly to make sure she can eat comfortably.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist says she needs regular check-ups to monitor her heart health. I try to stay on top of these appointments because I know how crucial they are for her well-being. It's always a relief when the results come back normal.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, she's been slower than her peers to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting. It was worrying at first, but with therapy and support, she's making progress. I'm just eager for her to catch up.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food textures can be a real issue for her. She's very picky and will only eat certain things if they're prepared in specific ways. Mealtime can be challenging, but we're learning to navigate her preferences.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... two main concerns. Firstly, her fontanelle took longer than usual to close completely. And secondly, her speech development isn't where it should be for her age. She doesn't speak as much as other children her age. Both these things worry me and I hope we can find ways to support her better.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular check-ups to monitor her heart health, as she needs to ensure her heart remains healthy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some require surgery, while others just need monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing and prefers certain food textures, which can be challenging for mealtime.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have difficulty chewing and prefer certain food textures, which can be challenging for mealtime.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower than peers to reach certain developmental milestones, including walking and sitting, and has shown signs of developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 90% of people with KBG syndrome have developmental delays, and some show behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a delayed closure of the soft spot on her head (anterior fontanelle) and has experienced feeding difficulties, which can lead to long-lasting lack of interest in feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means her eyes don't focus properly on things, and she has been concerned about how this might affect her learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Many children have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing and prefers certain food textures, which can be challenging for mealtime.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have difficulty chewing and prefer certain food textures, which can be challenging for mealtime.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower than peers to reach certain developmental milestones, including walking and sitting, and has shown signs of developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 90% of people with KBG syndrome have developmental delays, and some show behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), or anxiety.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows signs of developmental delay and behavioral differences, such as ASD, ADHD, or anxiety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 90% of people with KBG syndrome have developmental delays, and some show behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and has short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: To address the patient's difficulty chewing and preference for certain food textures.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5: To monitor the patient's hearing and rule out potential hearing loss.
c) Ophthalmology review: To assess the patient's astigmatism and ensure proper focusing of her eyes.
d) Palate review: To evaluate the patient's speech development and feeding difficulties, considering possible referral for specialist review.
e) Cardiac review: To monitor the patient's heart health and ensure her heart remains healthy.
f) Skeletal review: To assess the patient's unusual structure of her spinal bones and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.
g) Feeding assessment: To address the patient's feeding difficulties and mealtime challenges.
h) Management of tethered cord: To monitor the patient's sacral dimple and unusual gait associated with tethered cord.
i) Monitoring growth velocity: To track the patient's height and ensure it stays within the expected range.
j) Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy: To support the patient's overall development and address any specific needs.

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher-than-normal curvature of her cornea. This affects how she sees objects at different distances. She sometimes struggles with focusing, especially when looking at things close-up. 

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child had fluid buildup in her ears a couple of times. It affected her ability to hear clearly and caused discomfort. Thankfully, after treatment‚ it cleared up‚ but we monitor her ears regularly now.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth seem prone to chipping or breaking easier than they should. Even minor accidents can cause noticeable damage‚ so we have to ensure she’s extra careful during meals and playtime to avoid any incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Compared to other kids‚ she tires out faster during physical activities. While she can run around and have fun‚ we notice she needs breaks sooner than her friends do. It might be related to her overall energy levels rather than a specific heart condition‚ but we keep an eye on it.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she falls more frequently than other children her age. Whether it’s due to coordination or balance issues‚ we’re working with her to improve strength and agility to reduce these incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been challenging for her since infancy. Certain textures and tastes make mealtime difficult‚ and she has sensitivities to particular foods that trigger digestive discomfort.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned issues‚ our child moves slightly differently compared to her peers. There’s also a concern regarding delayed fontanelle closure‚ where certain bones in her skull took longer to fully close than typically expected. These aspects require periodic assessments to monitor progress and adjust care accordingly.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments. In a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our child requires close monitoring and periodic visits to the cardiologist due to a septal defect, which has been managed well with medication and lifestyle adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some require surgery, while others just need monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Feeding has indeed been challenging for our child; he experiences difficulties that affect his daily routine and overall nutrition intake. Managing mealtimes can be stressful due to these feeding issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. Lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our child appears to get tired more quickly than his peers during physical activities, suggesting there could be a neurodevelopmental aspect to consider. Detailed assessments would be needed to fully understand this symptom.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments. In a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: Our child often complains of squinting when trying to focus on objects or text, which suggests there might be an issue with his vision that needs addressing. We've noticed this happening more frequently over the past year, especially when he's doing homework or reading.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, which can occasionally be a feature.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: Our child has vision problems such as astigmatism, short-sightedness (myopia), and long-sightedness (hypermetropia). Squint (strabismus) can occasionally be a feature.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have vision problems such as astigmatism, short-sightedness (myopia), and long-sightedness (hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our child has a characteristic facial appearance, very large permanent teeth, and variable degrees of developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have a characteristic facial appearance, very large permanent teeth, and variable degrees of developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Our child's teeth seem to break or chip rather easily, and we've had to take extra precautions to ensure he doesn't bite into hard foods. Regular visits to the dentist are recommended to prevent further damage.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have teeth that break or chip rather easily.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: Our child needs extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have difficulty in school, needing extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: Our child often gets tired more quickly than his peers during physical activities, suggesting there could be a neurodevelopmental aspect to consider. Detailed assessments would be needed to fully understand this symptom.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have behavior differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: Our child has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle). Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle). Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Management Recommendations:
   - Regular dental check-ups
   - Regular hearing reviews to age 5 (even if earlier reviews give a clear response)
   - Ophthalmology review
   - Palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns)
   - Cardiac review (including echocardiogram and electrocardiogram) following diagnosis
   - Skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis
   - Monitoring growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile, refer for endocrine investigations
   - Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy

b) Medical Concerns:
   - Seizures: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments. In a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.
   - Hearing: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear (build-up of fluid in the ear), which can cause conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear. Many children have required multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some have still required hearing aids. Hearing should be carefully and regularly checked during the first few years.
   - Eyesight: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short-sightedness (myopia), and long-sightedness (hypermetropia). Squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, can occasionally be a feature.
   - Undescended testes: Many boys with KBG syndrome are born with testicles that have not completed their journey from the tummy (abdomen) to the sack (scrotum) (cryptorchidism). In some boys, the testes descend in due course on their own, but if they do not, they can be brought down and fixed in the scrotum with a simple surgical operation (orchidopexy).
   - Skeletal: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle). Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
   - Teeth: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns. Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important. It is important for children with KBG syndrome to have regular dental check-ups.
   - Feeding: Many babies have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. It is unique's experience that lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.
   - Cardiac: Most children with KBG syndrome do not have a very serious heart condition. However, a study of 40 European patients showed that 15/40 (38%) had heart conditions. These included changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. A few required surgery but some just needed monitoring.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing while playing, indicating potential respiratory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods and has difficulty swallowing, making meal times challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated when exposed to loud noises, suggesting possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means he has trouble seeing things far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods and has difficulty swallowing, making meal times challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has behavioral differences such as ASD, ADHD, or anxiety, requiring medication in some circumstances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

a) Regular dental check-ups: To ensure proper dental care and address any issues early.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5: To monitor hearing and provide timely intervention if needed.
c) Ophthalmology review: To check the patient's vision and address any vision-related challenges.
d) Check position of testes in boys: To rule out cryptorchidism and ensure normal testicular descent.

f) Referral for a cardiac review: Following diagnosis, considering echocardiography and electrocardiogram (ECG) to assess heart health.
g) Monitoring growth velocity: If height is below the 2nd centile, refer for endocrine investigations.
h) Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy: To address various functional impairments and improve overall quality of life.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... she has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things far away. We've gotten her glasses to help correct it, but it's still something we're monitoring closely.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes she doesn't respond right away when I call her name. It's like she's not paying attention or something. I worry that maybe there's a problem with her hearing, but the tests haven't shown anything conclusive yet.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: She complains about tooth sensitivity whenever she eats cold foods like ice cream or yogurt. It's become a big issue because she loves those things and gets really upset when she can't have them.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist found a structural abnormality in her heart. We go for regular check-ups to make sure everything is okay and that it doesn't affect her daily life too much.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Yes... she has epilepsy. We have to be very careful about her condition and ensure she takes her medication regularly to prevent seizures.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Actually, yes... she has a feeding aversion. There are certain textures and tastes she just won't tolerate, and it makes mealtime really challenging.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Well... developmentally, she seems behind other kids her age. It takes her longer to learn new skills and reach milestones. We're working with therapists to support her development and hoping she'll catch up soon.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in her heart, requiring regular check-ups to ensure it doesn't affect her daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, requiring careful monitoring and ensuring she takes her medication regularly to prevent seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty responding to calls and getting used to noises, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have hearing difficulties, including recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness, which can worsen speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have vision problems, including astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has tooth sensitivity, particularly to cold foods, leading to complaints about tooth sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have tooth sensitivity, and around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows developmental delays and requires additional help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome show developmental delays, and around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication may be appropriate in some circumstances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome exhibit behavioral differences, and around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, and around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have structural abnormalities of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: The patient needs regular dental check-ups to maintain proper oral health.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5: The patient should undergo regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for any hearing issues.
c) Ophthalmology review: The patient should have regular eye examinations to monitor for vision problems.
d) Palate review: The patient should be referred for a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
e) Cardiac review: The patient should undergo regular cardiac check-ups to ensure her heart condition doesn't affect her daily life.
f) Skeletal review: The patient should have X-rays of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull to assess bone age and detect any structural abnormalities.
g) Monitoring growth velocity: The patient's height should be monitored to ensure it stays within normal limits.
h) Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy: The patient should receive physical, occupational, speech, and behavior therapy to address her developmental delays and challenges.

Parent: Besides the issues already mentioned, our main concern is his speech delay. He's not speaking as much as we would expect for a child of his age. The specialists are looking into this and we're receiving support to help him catch up with his communication skills.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing when active compared to peers, potentially indicating underlying cardiovascular issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has bowel problems, getting constipated easily if not drinking enough water or eating the right foods, leading to dietary monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, affecting muscle tone, making her muscles feel stiff and needing physical therapy to improve.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle closed later than expected and takes longer to reach developmental milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, difficulty seeing things clearly unless they're really close up, and needs glasses to correct it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups to prevent further tooth problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), or anxiety, and medication may be appropriate in some circumstances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve changes, hole in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities, requiring monitoring or surgery.

a) Regular dental check-ups: To prevent further tooth problems.

g) Asymmetric hip creases in infancy and/or asymmetric or painful gait should prompt medical review.

i) Monitor growth velocity: If height is below the 2nd centile, refer for endocrine investigations within the context of familial heights.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect, which is being monitored closely to see if it requires surgery or can be managed with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's weight gain is slower compared to other kids her age, and meal times can be frustrating because she eats very little.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids her age, even on flat ground, and she trips over her own feet sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's hearing is impacted, leading to difficulty in responding to calls and occasional hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, squint, and treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go to the dentist a lot because of cavities and other tooth problems, and we are taking better care of her teeth at home.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems behind other children in development, noticeable in how she plays and interacts with others.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids her age, even on flat ground, and she trips over her own feet sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: The patient needs to go to the dentist a lot because of cavities and other tooth problems, and we are taking better care of her teeth at home.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5: The patient's hearing is impacted, leading to difficulty in responding to calls and occasional hearing loss, so hearing reviews should be conducted every year.
c) Ophthalmology review: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, squint, and treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.
d) Cardiac review: The patient has a septal defect, which is being monitored closely to see if it requires surgery or can be managed with medication.
e) Palate review: The patient has subtler anomalies affecting speech development and feeding, which may require referral for specialist review.
f) Skeletal review: X-rays of the wrist (to determine bone age), hip, spine, and skull should be taken in children following diagnosis.
g) Monitoring growth velocity: If the patient's height is below the 2nd centile, referral for endocrine investigations should be considered within the context of familial heights.
h) Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy: Management recommendations include physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions, which can lead to difficulty eating and swallowing.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities noted during exams, requiring close monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, which can affect the palate and speech development.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism and short-sightedness, which can worsen speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, which can affect the eyes and speech development.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, which can affect dental health.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, which can affect academic performance and social interactions.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits coordination issues, appearing less coordinated than other kids his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, which can affect brain function and coordination.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, which can affect skeletal development.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: To maintain proper dental hygiene and address any potential dental issues.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5: To ensure timely detection and treatment of hearing problems.
c) Ophthalmology review: To monitor vision and speech development.
d) Palate review: To assess any palatal abnormalities and their impact on speech and feeding.

f) Skeletal review: To evaluate the presence of scoliosis and other skeletal anomalies.
g) Monitoring growth velocity: To identify early signs of growth issues and refer for endocrine investigations if necessary.
h) Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy: To address coordination issues and improve overall functionality.

a) Regular dental check-ups: To ensure proper dental care and prevent tooth decay.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5: To detect and address hearing impairments early.

e) Cardiac review: Including echocardiography and electrocardiogram (ECG) to rule out heart conditions.
f) Skeletal review: X-rays of the wrist, hips, spine, and skull to evaluate bone age and identify any abnormalities.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with selective eating, refusing certain foods and becoming picky about what he eats, leading to potential nutritional deficiencies.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, indicating a high prevalence of medical concerns affecting neurology and overall health.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints when looking at things, especially when watching TV or playing video games, and may have difficulty understanding spoken words.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, indicating a high prevalence of medical concerns affecting the ears, nose, and throat.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism, short-sightedness, and long-sightedness, which can lead to speech delays and difficulty speaking clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, indicating a high prevalence of medical concerns affecting the eyes and overall health.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, indicating a high prevalence of medical concerns affecting skin and overall health.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th finger (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, indicating a high prevalence of medical concerns affecting skeletal development and overall health.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with feeding, getting constipated or having loose stools, and requires dietary adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 15% have heart conditions, including structural abnormalities.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord, which needs ongoing monitoring by the neurologists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including structural abnormalities.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a delayed closure of the soft spot on her head (anterior fontanelle) and suboptimal positioning of her testes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, squint, and treatment options like patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including structural abnormalities.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a shortened index finger (brachydactyly) with a curved fifth finger (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including structural abnormalities.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, making her teeth more susceptible to cavities and sensitivity, and requires careful toothbrushing and limiting sugary food intake.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including structural abnormalities.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional help in school, especially in mainstream secondary school, and may need specialized schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including structural abnormalities.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including structural abnormalities.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, leading to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the fifth finger (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including structural abnormalities.
